items.title: Charles Elgar Interview, 1958-05-27
items.q: Lorenzo Jr., I've seen him. He had sort of long, black, wavy hair.

ctx.x: Yeah, but they didn't even have the Spanish accent. They didn't even have that? No. But when you saw them, you know you were looking at a Mexican. They had, you know, they're a certain type.
I've never even seen a good picture of them. No? Lorenzo Jr., I've seen him. He had sort of long, black, wavy hair. Uh-huh. A real good-looking fellow. A great big fellow.
Oh, yeah, they both were. But how were they? And I can't, I don't know that I've ever seen a picture of the old man.

items.title: Charles Elgar Interview, 1958-05-27
items.q: And I sent for Emmanuel Perez, Lorenzo Teal, Louis Cottrell, and I brought an outfit here to work for Mike Fritzel.

ctx.x: Uh-huh. Just a little before the war. Because just about that time, I went, I was playing at the Washington Theater here, 31st and State. And I sent for Emmanuel Perez, Lorenzo Teal, Louis Cottrell, and I brought an outfit here to work for Mike Fritzel. Yes. At that time, Mike Fritzel had a place on Madison and Paulina. Was that the Ansonia? The Ansonia, that's right. And I put them in the Ansonia for Mike. And I had intended, as the orchestra developed, I had intended to take the move over with me. But they were…
Excuse me for interrupting your train of thought, but is Mike Fritzel still here, you think? No, Mike died.
